sections.theory:
(b) IUPAC Nomenclature

Aliphatic monocarboxylic acids are named as alkanoic acids. These are obtained by replacing the ending ‘–e’ of the corresponding alkane with the suffix ‘–oic acid’ e.g.

In case of branched acids, the chain is numbered starting from the carboxyl carbon atom and substituents are located in the usual way. Carboxylic acids containing two carboxyl groups are named as alkanedioic acid; their trivial names are also given in parenthesis. Similarly, the unsaturated carboxylic acids are named as alkenoic acid, alkynoic acid (examples shown above).

If carboxyl group is attached to a cyclic ring, it is named by adding suffix –carboxylic acid to name of cycloalkane.

Nomenclature of acid halides

The names of acid halides are derived from the names of corresponding carboxylic acids. The ending –ic of the name of acid is replaced by –yl, and the word acid is replaced by halide, in both common and IUPAC systems.

sections.headingUrdu: امائیڈز، ایسٹرز، این ہائیڈرائیڈز اور نائٹرائلز کی نام گذاری
sections.headingPashto: د امایډونو، ایسټرونو، انهایدرایډونو او نایټرایلونو نومول

paras.text: Names of amides are also derived from carboxylic acids. The ending –ic acid of common names and –oic acid from IUPAC name is replaced by –amide.
